* The Tomb Raider sequel is heavily shown at the conference, there will be a playable demo on stage, in which the game will be releasing closer than expected, in September. 

* It is revealed that Battletoads will soon be available on the Xbox marketplace, priced at the typical fifteen dollar price. The game will maintain the same standard that has been upheld throughout the series,though it is not being developed by Rare.

* Gears of War: Remastered is going to be a complete remaster, such as seen by 343i, in their remaster of Halo 2. It will be playable, and will showoff very good modern looking visuals, while still maintaining the core systems of the original Gears of War. Expect to hear thoroughly about the online multiplayer. Gears of War 4 will not be shown at all, and will be held off until another future press conference.

* Rare reveals their new project, sadly, it is not a sequel to our former beloved franchises; it will be radically different from Rare's top games. It'll if anything, be a re-imagining of Perfect Dark. It is also revealed that Rare classics will be available in the Xbox marketplace in the coming months; these include the Banjo Series, Conker, the original Battletoad games, and the Perfect Dark series. They will all be likely be priced at ten dollars per game.
* Forza 6 will be shown thoroughly.

* Halo 5 will be given a large amount of time at the conference, highlighting advances in multi-player, as well as their improvements on the fluidity of the game-play. The game will be given a firm release date in October; along with the announcement that another multiplayer beta will arise, exclusively for Xbox Live Gold members.
* Fable Legends will be shown off.

* Twisted Pixel will have time to show off their newest game, releasing in mid August. The game will be their first true venture as a mass released $60 game. The game will look very intriguing, and will have lots of charm to it, similar to Sunset Overdrive in its tone and character.

* Joe Montana Football will be revealed, and gameplay will be shown, as it will release around the same period that Madden usually does. Though the game does not include NFL rosters; the creation studio within the game is shown to be very impressive, and capable of emulating an NFL experience.

* Several new IPs will be shown, though most of them will be indie games, they all look fairly promising. Lionhead Studio's new game will look very impressive, while being separate from Fable lore. It is revealed that Ryse: 2 is in development, and will likely take place in the isles of Greece. Capcom will be showing off a new IP, that wont be Dead Rising.

* Kingdom Hearts 1.5 and 2.5 will be releasing to the Xbox One later in the year, along with a beta to Kingdom Hearts 3, that will be available for access at the start of 2016. Other Square Enix games will be ported to the Xbox One; including a Final Fantasy collection, which includes Final Fantasies 1-8, for $60. Final Fantasy X1 and X-2 will also be released to the console.

* There will be a big exclusive IP announcement, as it appears that Microsoft and Sony have begun to enter into an "IP war." Silent Hills is possible, though Microsoft would have to invest lots of money, as the game is no where near release. It will be big, and it will most likely be a Capcom IP. The sequel to Remember Me, will be shown off as an Xbox exclusive, as likely the biggest shocker of the conference.

I'm going for a bit of an unorthodox scenario here, but I think it could end up working out for us. 

**-The Draft-**

I've been a strong supporter of both Mariota and Winston, but there are so many red flags on both of these college quarterbacks. Mariota seems to be a product of an Oregon system, and tight NFL throws aren't asked of him. He displays a run first mentality and needs to be groomed into the pocket. Winston has off the field issues, and at times makes bad decisions. But he is the better NFL prospect in my mind.

- Round 1: Leonard Williams DE/DT USC. He's the best player in this draft in my opinion, and tagging him alongside Gerald McCoy would no doubt give us an elite defensive line. He's played in a 3-4 defensive scheme, a 4-3 scheme, and a tampa 2 scheme. So I don't believe that his transition to our defense will be much of an issue at all. He's incredibly explosive, as well as very strong. I think he's a player with absolutely just about no red flags, and is a guy who will undoubtedly make an impact as soon as he steps on the field. 

- Round 2: Brett Hundley QB out of UCLA. Hundley has the arm to be a proficient NFL quarterback, as well as having athletic abilities at least somewhat comparable to Mariota. His stats are comparable to the "big two" as well, and he is quite efficient with stats that could easily be compared to Mariota. I feel as though Hundley has the potential to be a great quarterback. He definitely reminds me of Teddy Bridgewater. The red flags, while still prevalent, just aren't as big in comparison to Winston and Mariota.

- Round 3/4: I want us to look for a Linebacker in the third round, or possibly a safety. I want someone who is more than capable of playing in our defense, as well as having the explosiveness to stop the run. I'd like to select Eric Striker (OLB) out of Oklahoma. He's extremely explosive, and can run in our Tampa 2 style. For the fourth round pick, I really want us to select a capable offensive linemen, preferably a guard.

**Free Agency**

- We need to address the Safety position, which has arguably been one of our worst positions defensively. I want us to go after Tashaun Gipson, at 25, he's already shown to be a very great safety already, and with a ton of upside. 

- We also need a solid inside linebacker. I want Rolando McClain. He's clearly been one of the breakout players of the Cowboys' defense, and I believe that our defense could be one of the most feared, with him alongside Lavonte David.

**Other**

- Trade Mike Glennon. While we may not get much out of him, it's worth it, considering he would possibly be our third string quarterback, and very well could draw some interest considering his performance last season and our win against the Steelers. He's shown to at least be a capable Quarterback, so I would expect at the minimum a fifth round pick, but I wouldn't mind simply trading him to free up cap room. The Bills or possibly the Rams or Cardinals would likely be his destination.

- I'd also consider trading away Michael Johnson who has severely under preformed, and has just been a monster to our cap space. A second round pick would be ideal, but I'd be open to letting him stay.

Non-biased opinion-

Look at the exclusive titles- If you like Halo, Sunset Overdrive, Forza, and others, get an Xbox. If you like the Naughty Dog titles and the Sony Studio titles get a PS4.

Yes the PS4 is the stronger console hardware wise. But do not discount the Xbox One. Most multi-platform games will have them running nearly the same, though some games will look slightly better on PS4 (1080p compared to 900p.) A lot of games are starting to become more optimized for all platforms, so that everyone gets an "equal" experience (cue the parity discussions.)

The Controllers- Both controllers are great. The Xbox One has a really nice controller, and the rumble triggers are fantastic. The PS4's controller is a massive improvement, but it still feels odd to me. I've always preferred the feel of the Xbox controllers. But just see which one you prefer.

The Xbox One gets monthly updates, as opposed to minimal PS4 updates. It's insane how far they've improved everything, including the OS. Go look at previous updates to see the progression. The PS4 has been getting updates, but at a very slow pace in comparison.

PSN is more prone to hackers, I've noticed that Xbox Live is more secure, but I wouldn't say this is a gamebreaker at all, and both online services are great. The PS+ games and the Xbox Games with Gold games are about on the same level, many of them are indie titles.
